description: After each repair, greedily grow every radius to the largest value its neighbours and the walls allow, in seeded random order, repeating until no radius changes by more than 1e-12 (capped at 1000 passes).
Pass per-variable bounds to SLSQP (centres in [0, 1], radii in [0, 0.5]) so the box limits are handled natively instead of only through inequality constraints, keeping the constraint count lower.
Restrict the SLSQP pair constraints to each circle's k=8 nearest neighbours (symmetrised), recomputed from the starting centres at each SLSQP call, instead of all n(n-1)/2 pairs.
Precompute the triu pair indices once in solve and, per restart, keep only the pair constraints whose initial centres are closer than a cutoff (0.5), so SLSQP handles fewer constraints per step.

Every third SLSQP restart adds a -0.01 * sum(log boundary gap) term to the objective to push centres away from the walls, while the other restarts keep -sum(r), and the best packing is still chosen by true radius sum.

Replace the SLSQP call in _solve_once with a sequential LP trust-region loop (linprog/highs on linearised pair and wall constraints, merit = min(0, min gap), delta halved on rejection and grown by 1.5 up to 0.1), starting from zero radii so the start is feasible.
Half of the restarts after the first start from the incumbent with its smallest-radius circle moved to the largest empty spot (200x200 grid) at a tiny radius, then re-optimised with SLSQP.

Adds a basin-hopping phase after the first half of the time budget: perturb the best packing's centres with a Gaussian scale decaying linearly from 0.1 to 0.005, re-optimise with SLSQP from the perturbed start, and keep the result if its repaired radius sum is higher.

Adds a basin-hopping phase after the first half of the time budget: perturb the best packing's centres with a Gaussian scale decaying linearly from 0.1 to 0.005, re-optimise with SLSQP from the perturbed start, and keep the result if its repaired radius sum is higher.
Spend the first 40% of the CPU budget on random restarts with SLSQP capped at 60 iterations, then refine the top 3 packings in turn with 400 iterations for the remaining time.

In _solve_once, when there is no start, first solve an (n-1)-circle packing with SLSQP at half the iteration budget, insert one circle at the grid point with the largest free clearance (min of distance to centres minus radii, and wall distance) with a small radius, then run SLSQP on all n circles; repair, restarts and basin hopping are unchanged.

Initialise each SLSQP restart's centres by drawing 20n random points, taking n of them, and running 30 Lloyd iterations against a fixed 60x60 sample grid, so the starting centres are spread out (radii still start at INIT_RADIUS).

Draw the initial centre margin per restart uniformly from [0.02, 0.2] instead of the fixed INIT_LOW = 0.1, so starts range from corner-packed to central.

issues: Candidate has only 1 run against 2 incumbent runs. The +0.0009 improvement in mean radius sum is well under the noise sd of 0.0034, so z of about 0.22 gives no evidence of a gain and reject is correct.
Recomputed z = 0.0009 / (0.0034*sqrt(1/1+1/2)) = 0.216, consistent with the reported 0.212 (difference is likely rounding of the means).
No integrity problems: no file or network access, no hard-coded coordinates, and randomness still comes from the seeded rng.

I checked the penalty gradient by hand and it is correct (overlap, wall, negative-radius and radius-sum terms). The final answer still goes through SLSQP and the repair step, so validity is preserved.
The L-BFGS-B pre-relaxation runs only on random starts (start is None). It adds cost to each restart, but the restart loop still stops at 80% of the time budget, so the 45 s limit is not at risk.

description: Before SLSQP on a fresh random start, run three stages of L-BFGS-B on a penalty objective (negative radius sum plus growing-weight quadratic penalties on overlaps and boundary violations, with an analytic gradient) and pass the result as the SLSQP start.
Replace the SLSQP random-restart starts with a Lubachevsky-style Monte Carlo jamming start (random centres, radii grown per sweep with a shrinking move size), which SLSQP then refines and repairs.

For a random half of the fresh restarts, run SLSQP on n//2 free circles mirrored through (0.5, 0.5) (plus a centre circle for odd n), then polish the full 3n-variable packing with unconstrained SLSQP, leaving repair and best-of-restarts selection unchanged.

For a random half of the fresh restarts, run SLSQP on n//2 free circles mirrored through (0.5, 0.5) (plus a centre circle for odd n), then polish the full 3n-variable packing with unconstrained SLSQP, leaving repair and best-of-restarts selection unchanged.
Replaces the uniform random-restart phase with successive halving: batches of 8 SLSQP runs, sorted by radius sum, where the top 2 seed the next batch as perturbed starts.
Abort: the proposed change is already in train.py, since every candidate is repaired before its radius sum is compared.

Before the existing shrink loop in _repair, solve an LP with the centres fixed that maximises the sum of radii subject to pairwise and wall constraints (HiGHS), keeping the old repair as a safety fallback for tolerance residue.

Keep an elite pool of the best 5 packings across random restarts, and with probability 0.5 start each restart from a random elite packing with centres perturbed by Gaussian noise of scale 0.02, otherwise start uniform random.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels. It only adds analytic gradients for SLSQP.

I checked the constraint Jacobian against cons() row by row: the pair rows (u, -u, -1, -1), the four wall rows and the r >= 0 rows all match the order used in cons(). This assumes the hidden line computing d is dist - r_i - r_j, as in the incumbent. Clamping the distance at 1e-12 avoids division by zero. The objective gradient (-1 on each radius) is correct. The repair step after the solver still guarantees a valid packing, so even a wrong gradient could not produce an invalid result.

Recomputed z = (2.9334 - 2.9329) / (0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) ≈ 0.0005 / 0.00416 ≈ 0.12. The reported 0.127 differs only slightly, probably because the harness used unrounded values. The gain of 0.0005 is well inside the noise, so rejecting the candidate is reasonable.

The candidate has only one run. Exact gradients mainly make each SLSQP call faster, which allows more restarts in the same time. That benefit may be real but too small to see at this noise level. Rerun it only if it is cheap and gets combined with something else, such as more restarts or a larger MAX_ITER.

issues: No integrity problems: the grid starts are computed in code, there is no file access or pasted packing, all randomness comes from the seeded generator, and the repair step still runs.

Recomputed z = (2.9349-2.9329)/(0.0034*sqrt(1+1/2)) = 0.0020/0.00416 ~= 0.48. The harness reports 0.485; the small gap is most likely rounding of the displayed means. A single candidate run within noise: reject stands.
Misleading name: _sym_centres / sym give a jittered grid around the centre, not a symmetric start.
With sym on, every restart starts from nearly the same grid (0.01 jitter), so extra restarts may add little.
The coin flip that picks the mode is drawn once per seed and shifts the rest of the seed's random draws, so the two start modes are compared on different seeds.
Grid starts are clipped to [0, 1] instead of kept off the edges by INIT_LOW. Harmless, because the bounds and the repair step keep the packing valid.

description: With probability one half per seed, the fresh SLSQP restarts start from a jittered centred square grid of centres instead of uniform random centres, and the basin-hopping phase is unchanged.

Before the random-restart SLSQP phase, screen 64 random starts with 200 steps of decaying gradient descent on a quadratic overlap-plus-wall penalty (vectorised over all starts), then run SLSQP and repair only on the best 3 by repaired radius sum.
After each SLSQP centre solve, freeze the centres and polish the radii with a radius-only SLSQP, then run one more centre pass followed by another radius polish.

Keep an elite pool of the 4 best packings, build crossover children (a random line splits two parents, with the count fixed to n) as SLSQP starts during the first half of the budget, and update the pool after every restart and basin-hopping step.
